Check: Confirm the process is the approved agent
Evidence to capture: Path; filename; publisher signature; version; service; parent process; tenant; device ID
Common interpretation: Filename alone can match an impostor or stale component
Safe next action: Validate identity before performance remediation
Escalation trigger: Unexpected path; signature failure; wrong tenant; or suspicious parent

Check: Record business scope and impact
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; device; workload; impact; observation window; production criticality
Common interpretation: A symptom without scope cannot justify fleet action
Safe next action: Define authority; maintenance window; stop condition; and communication
Escalation trigger: Production impact or authority is unclear

Check: Determine whether one endpoint or a shared cohort is affected
Evidence to capture: Affected count; OS; agent version; policy; job; patch window; security stack; first observed time
Common interpretation: Shared attributes suggest regression or scheduled workload
Safe next action: Group by common attributes before per-device repair
Escalation trigger: Multiple customers; sites; or versions are affected

Check: Contain only the narrow approved workload when required
Evidence to capture: Paused job or policy; approver; start time; impact; expiry; compensating control
Common interpretation: Broad disablement hides the cause and removes protection
Safe next action: Pause the smallest justified workload with an expiry
Escalation trigger: Fleet-wide security or monitoring disablement is proposed

Check: Capture separated timestamped CPU samples
Evidence to capture: Sample times; interval; raw and normalized CPU; logical processor count
Common interpretation: One point-in-time value or screenshot cannot prove sustained CPU
Safe next action: Collect a bounded time series over a defined workload
Escalation trigger: CPU remains high with no identifiable workload

Check: Record process resource and identity fields
Evidence to capture: PID; start time; CPU; working set; private bytes; commit; handles; threads; read/write rates
Common interpretation: Memory and CPU labels describe different resource states
Safe next action: Preserve the baseline before restart or repair
Escalation trigger: PID churn; crash loop; handle growth; or private-memory growth

Check: Use a stable counter instance
Evidence to capture: Process V2 or PID mapping; duplicate process names; sample continuity
Common interpretation: Legacy Process instances can be remapped when same-name processes change
Safe next action: Use PID-aware or Process V2 collection where available
Escalation trigger: Measurements cannot be tied to one stable process

Check: Compare process use with host-wide pressure
Evidence to capture: Total CPU; available memory; commit; paging; disk latency; free space
Common interpretation: Host saturation can make a healthy agent appear causal
Safe next action: Resolve system-wide constraint or competing workload first
Escalation trigger: Kernel; storage; paging; or system-wide CPU pressure dominates

Check: Align the spike with scheduled agent activity
Evidence to capture: Patch scan; inventory; script; remote session; backup; AV scan; update; startup; policy refresh
Common interpretation: A bounded spike may be expected for a defined task
Safe next action: Compare duration and result with documented acceptance limits
Escalation trigger: Workload repeats; overlaps; or never reaches completion

Check: Check for retrying external dependencies
Evidence to capture: Destination; DNS; proxy; TLS; authentication; status code; retry interval
Common interpretation: Tight retries can drive CPU; memory; disk; and network use
Safe next action: Repair the verified dependency or vendor-supported backoff path
Escalation trigger: Unknown destination; credential issue; or platform incident

Check: Review agent and operating-system logs
Evidence to capture: Failure-window logs; first error; crash; update; cache; timeout; access denial; queue state
Common interpretation: Logs can distinguish useful work from repeated failure
Safe next action: Correlate the earliest relevant error before remediation
Escalation trigger: Logs are missing; altered; or show suspicious privileged activity

Check: Review security-control interaction
Evidence to capture: EDR; antivirus; content filter; application-control event; hash; signer; policy; time
Common interpretation: Repeated scanning or blocking can amplify agent workload
Safe next action: Validate artifacts and use a narrow approved exception only if justified
Escalation trigger: Malware suspicion; unsigned component; or fleet-wide block

Check: Inspect process tree; modules; handles; threads; and signer
Evidence to capture: Process Explorer capture or equivalent; owner; time; PID; process tree; modules; handles
Common interpretation: The hot thread or leaking handle may belong to a child or injected component
Safe next action: Capture read-only evidence before changing the process
Escalation trigger: Unknown module; signer mismatch; or suspicious injection

Check: Capture a bounded CPU trace when needed
Evidence to capture: WPR profile; start and end time; workload; ETL path; size; consent; storage location
Common interpretation: Sampled stacks can show where CPU time is spent
Safe next action: Use CPU Usage and add only symptom-relevant profiles
Escalation trigger: Trace contains customer data or requires vendor engineering

Check: Measure memory growth with the right model
Evidence to capture: Working set; private bytes; commit; allocation profile; handle count; time series
Common interpretation: Working set is not the same as private or committed memory
Safe next action: Choose heap; VirtualAlloc; resident-set; or handle evidence for a defined question
Escalation trigger: Unbounded growth; paging; allocation failure; or host instability

Check: Create a dump only when authorized and necessary
Evidence to capture: Reason; approver; trigger; PID; capture time; size; encryption; access; retention; transfer
Common interpretation: A dump can enable root-cause analysis but may contain sensitive memory
Safe next action: Use the smallest justified dump and secure handling process
Escalation trigger: Credentials; customer data; regulated data; or incident suspicion may be present

Check: Define success; stop; rollback; and retention before change
Evidence to capture: Expected CPU and memory boundary; observation window; functions to test; rollback; owner
Common interpretation: Unbounded repair cannot prove improvement
Safe next action: Write the acceptance and rollback plan first
Escalation trigger: No safe rollback for a production-critical endpoint

Check: Correct the verified narrow cause
Evidence to capture: Cause; vendor guidance; change; actor; time; output; version or policy
Common interpretation: Failed update; damaged cache; retry loop; conflict; or unsupported build needs targeted repair
Safe next action: Use the vendor-supported repair path on one endpoint
Escalation trigger: Cause remains unknown or requires broad exclusions

Check: Test one authorized restart or repair
Evidence to capture: Before and after PID; version; signature; samples; logs; task results; audit record
Common interpretation: A restart can mask recurrence without fixing the cause
Safe next action: Retest through the same workload and observation window
Escalation trigger: Symptom returns; identity changes; or functions fail

Check: Control any exclusion or throttle
Evidence to capture: Scope; justification; approver; compensating control; start; expiry; review; rollback
Common interpretation: Permanent broad exclusions create hidden operational and security debt
Safe next action: Use a scoped time-bounded exception with retest
Escalation trigger: Fleet-wide; permanent; or unowned exception is requested

Check: Repeat comparable performance measurements
Evidence to capture: Same counters; workload; interval; host pressure; version; policy; timestamps
Common interpretation: Only comparable before and after evidence can show improvement
Safe next action: Compare against the documented acceptance boundary
Escalation trigger: Measurement window or workload is not comparable

Check: Verify agent functions separately
Evidence to capture: Fresh heartbeat; inventory; alert; bounded script; patch scan; remote-session audit
Common interpretation: Low resource use can mean a disabled or partially broken agent
Safe next action: Open owned work for each failed function
Escalation trigger: Privileged function fails or produces no audit evidence

Check: Reconcile the affected cohort
Evidence to capture: Recovered; unaffected; still impacted; retired; duplicate; wrong version; unknown; exception counts
Common interpretation: A one-device fix does not prove fleet recovery
Safe next action: Assign an owner and due date to every unresolved endpoint
Escalation trigger: Unknown or cross-customer records remain

Check: Record cause; prevention; residual risk; and closure
Evidence to capture: Root cause; affected version or policy; corrective action; prevention; owner; review date; customer acceptance
Common interpretation: Recurring overhead usually exposes a monitoring; rollout; dependency; or change-control gap
Safe next action: Update runbooks; alerts; pilot gates; and evidence retention
Escalation trigger: Residual risk lacks approval; owner; or expiry
